# Chapter 6 — sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) The requirement (NIS2 Art. 21, GDPR Art. 32) obliges protection but names
no measures; the catalogue (A.8.5) supplies the named, checkable control; the
organisation judges how strongly to implement it, proportionate to its risk. (2)
Technical: Encryption of the database (A.8.24) --- preventive. Process: A
periodic access review of who can reach the database --- detective. People:
Training staff who handle customer data (A.6.3) --- preventive. (A corrective
complement: Restore from backup.) (3) Yes in substance: A.8.5 (MFA) and A.8.24
(encryption) sit under Protect in the CSF mapping, as does the awareness
training. Because the frameworks map onto each other, the same implementation
evidence --- configurations, logs --- answers the CSF question without any new
work. (4) Tailoring fits the control's purpose to the organisation's risk and
size: FastGoods' alerts-plus-weekly-review detects incidents in time to act, at
proportionate cost, which is what the control requires; a bank's SOC answers a
bank's risk, not a webshop's. The variant that fails is alerts sent to an unread
mailbox --- the purpose (timely detection) is not met, however configured the
tooling. (5) Control: A.8.13 / backup (or, from this chapter's tables, the
corrective complement to A.8.24). Applies: Yes. Justification: Treats R3's
impact and enables restoration (GDPR Art. 32 names restore capability). Status:
Implemented. Evidence: Backup job logs and a documented restore test. It treats
R3 --- and, by restoring availability, softens R2's worst case too.
